headers.//: Vite emits content-hashed filenames under /assets, so those bytes can never change under a given URL. Immutable caching is what makes the hashed names worth having: the browser skips revalidation entirely on a repeat visit.

index.html is the one unhashed file that points at hashed chunks. It must be revalidated on every navigation: a cached shell referencing a deleted chunk is a white screen, and that is the failure mode hashed assets + long TTLs would otherwise create.
The three root SVGs live in public/ and keep a stable name across builds, so they cannot be immutable. A short TTL with revalidation is the safe middle ground.
